input.quote: which shall be no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million.
input.rationale: Section 4.2.3(ii) imposes a floor: PB must elect at least $110 million of Development Costs to be funded by SFJ, and that election drives PB's downstream Approval Payments (up to $600 million, pro-rated to actual Development Costs under Section 6.2). That is a minimum commitment on us with no reduction mechanic: it is not limited to a current 12-month period, cannot be reduced on 30 days' notice, and the only exit (Section 14.2.2 at-will termination) requires payment of 300% of Development Costs incurred, which is a penalty rather than a true-up. It therefore fails the fallback on material terms. We take the preferred position with the shortest edit - deleting the $110 million floor while leaving the $120 million ceiling and the rest of the election mechanic untouched; Section 6.2 already ensures we pay only in proportion to the Development Costs actually funded. We have not touched the allocation of overruns to PB (Sections 4.1, 4.2.2, 4.2.3) or the use-of-funds covenant in Section 4.2.3, which are cost-allocation terms rather than purchase or volume commitments.

ops.oldText: which shall be no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million.
ops.newText: which shall be no more than $120 million, with no minimum amount.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the $110 million floor on the Elected Total Amount so we have no minimum commitment and can elect only the funding we actually need; Section 6.2 already scales the Approval Payments to the Development Costs actually funded. If SFJ needs a floor, we could look at one limited to the current 12-month period and reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up.
proposal.summary: Remove the $110 million floor on the Elected Total Amount so PB has no minimum funding commitment.

mappings.quote: the Approval Payments will be multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is such actual amount of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ hereunder (as adjusted, to the extent applicable, pursuant to Section 2.3.3, Section 3.12.2 and/or Section 3.12.3) and the denominator of which is One Hundred Twenty Million U.S. Dollars ($120,000,000.00).
